title: Persistent Systems Reports Rs 483 Crore Q1 Profit as Nagarro Deal Dominates Outlook
excerpt: The mid-tier IT firm's net profit rose 13.7% year-on-year but fell 9% sequentially, as the spotlight shifts to its transformative $2.9 billion Nagarro acquisition.
body:
• Net profit rose 13.7% YoY to Rs 483 crore in Q1 FY27 but fell roughly 9% sequentially from Q4's Rs 529 crore
  • Revenue surged 29% YoY to an estimated Rs 4,300 crore, with the company posting record deal wins during the quarter
  • The $1.3 billion Nagarro acquisition, targeting a $2.9 billion combined entity, aims for $5 billion revenue by FY31

Persistent Systems reported a 13.7% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 483 crore for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27), with revenue jumping 29% from the year-ago period. The Pune-based IT services company also posted record deal wins during the quarter, though investor attention remained largely trained on its proposed $1.3 billion takeover of German digital engineering firm Nagarro SE.

While the year-on-year profit trajectory looks healthy, net profit fell about 9% sequentially from Q4 FY26's Rs 529.26 crore—a pattern consistent with typical first-quarter seasonal effects including annual wage hikes and new-year client budget resets.

Context

The June quarter results build on an already strong FY26, during which Persistent delivered $1.65 billion in annual revenue—up 17.4% year-on-year in dollar terms—with an EBIT margin of 15.6%. The company was recognised by Brand Finance as the fastest-growing IT services brand globally in 2026.

Growth in Q1 FY27 was anchored by the same verticals that have driven Persistent's outperformance: BFSI, software and hi-tech, and healthcare and life sciences. In the year-ago quarter, BFSI had grown 30.7% YoY, while healthcare—after a brief wobble—has been rebounding on the back of data-led transformation projects and AI adoption.

"Our approach has consistently been to build capabilities ahead of demand. Over the past 36 years, we have invested in strengthening our engineering depth and data foundations, which are now finding greater application as AI adoption scales across enterprises."

— Dr. Anand Deshpande, Founder, Chairman and Managing Director, Persistent Systems

The Nagarro Deal Casts a Long Shadow

But the headline story for Persistent Systems is not standalone earnings—it is the proposed acquisition of Nagarro SE, announced on June 28. The all-cash deal offers EUR 81 per share, a 140% premium over Nagarro's undisturbed closing price, and would create a combined entity with approximately $2.9 billion in revenue and over 46,000 employees across more than 40 countries—including roughly 37,000 in India.

Persistent has already secured about 21% of Nagarro's shares through a binding agreement with its largest shareholder, Lantano Beteiligungen, and is making a voluntary public offer for the remainder. The minimum acceptance threshold is 50%. The deal is funded through a EUR 1.4 billion facility from Barclays, with the company aiming to significantly deleverage within two years through internal cash generation.

Nagarro—which reported EUR 248 million in Q1 2026 revenue with 6.5% constant-currency growth—brings SAP implementation expertise, an OpenAI partnership, and a strong European footprint that Persistent has long coveted. CEO Sandeep Kalra noted during an analyst call that Nagarro is "a key implementation partner for SAP, whereas our ERP progress is not necessarily at scale," according to Mint. Kalra attributed Nagarro's recent revenue slowdown to temporary distractions from an earlier effort to take the company private.

The combined entity would vault Persistent to become India's seventh-largest IT services company, up two spots from its current position.

Impact

Brokerages remain sharply divided on the deal's merits. CLSA maintained a high-conviction outperform rating with a target price of Rs 6,520, arguing the acquisition could be about 6% EPS accretive at the current purchase price. The brokerage noted that Nagarro's annual revenue of $1.14 billion represents about 69% of Persistent's FY26 revenue, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. PL Capital reiterated a buy at Rs 6,400, while Motilal Oswal also held its buy rating.

On the other side, Citi retained a sell rating with a Rs 4,090 target, calling the deal expensive given Nagarro's historical growth trajectory and current global valuations. Kotak Securities maintained a reduce rating at Rs 4,700, and Equirus also flagged valuation concerns with a Rs 5,010 target.

One key concern: Nagarro's operating margin of 10.9% in FY25 significantly trails Persistent's 15.6%. Management has pushed back, saying combined margins would not fall below Persistent's current level, citing planned cost synergies and the potential to rationalise tail accounts.

What's Next

The Nagarro acquisition is expected to close by late 2026 or early 2027, pending regulatory clearance from the German market regulator and the outcome of the open offer. Management has set a target of $5 billion in annual revenue by March 2031 for the combined Persistent-Nagarro Group—implying a compound annual growth rate of roughly 12% from the combined revenue base.

More immediately, investors will watch whether the record deal wins in Q1 translate into accelerated revenue growth in the coming quarters, and how Persistent manages the integration challenge while maintaining its own organic growth momentum. The company expects European revenue to rise to 22% of total revenue from 10% currently, with significant expansion planned in BFSI and telecom verticals where the combined entity would earn an estimated $750 million each, according to Mint.

For a company that started FY25 with $1.4 billion in revenue and is now on track to cross $3 billion upon deal completion, the growth story is compelling—if it can execute without diluting margins or taking on unsustainable leverage.
